name: Glow & Lovely

card.summary: A mass-market South Asian face cream, formerly Fair & Lovely, marketed for a brighter, more even-toned complexion.
card.note: Older mercury-containing lightening creams from other brands have documented toxicity; check ingredient labels and local regulations.

quick.overview:
Glow & Lovely is a face cream sold by Hindustan Unilever, first launched in India in 1975 as Fair & Lovely. It is positioned to give a brighter, more even-looking complexion, and its main active ingredient is niacinamide (vitamin B3), alongside vitamins C and E, glycerin and UV filters [3][4].

In 2020 the company dropped "Fair" from the name and moved its messaging to "glow" and "even tone". Published studies on the brand itself are mostly toxicology work on mercury content in older formulations and small imaging studies; the brand's cultural role, including criticism that it promotes colorism, is widely covered [3][5].
quick.how: Users apply it as a daily face cream, often as part of a basic routine, and the range now includes face washes, serums, BB cream and SPF variants. The brand says users look for an even, radiant tone, and gradual change over several weeks is what proponents describe [3][4].
quick.risks: Lab studies in mice on older, low-mercury Fair & Lovely samples reported mercury accumulation and tissue changes, although the content was below FDA limits [6][7]. Hindustan Unilever has attributed a 2020 Norwegian restriction to counterfeit products [4]. Critics also raise social concerns about colorism [3][8].

lead: Glow & Lovely is a skin-brightening cream from Hindustan Unilever, launched in India in 1975 under the name Fair & Lovely and renamed in July 2020. People use it to even out skin tone and give the face a lighter, more radiant look [3][4].

The company states that the formula contains niacinamide (vitamin B3), vitamins C and E, glycerin and sunscreen filters [3][4]. The range includes creams, face washes, serums, BB cream and SPF versions, and a men's line is sold as Glow & Handsome [4].

Published research on the brand is limited. A small laser biospeckle imaging study measured skin blood flow after applying several creams [1], and toxicology studies in mice examined mercury in older Fair & Lovely samples [6][7][9]. A 2025 qualitative study explored how the pressure to be "Fair and Lovely" relates to body image among British South Asian women [10].

chain: Niacinamide and vitamin-based cream applied daily
Supports brighter-looking, more even skin tone
angle.text: Users apply the cream as a daily moisturizer aiming for a more even, luminous face. The company describes niacinamide as the main active and now markets the effect as glow and even tone [3][4].

infobox: Creams, face washes, serums, BB cream, SPF

paras: The company says the formula contains niacinamide, vitamins C and E, glycerin and UVA/UVB sunscreens, with additions such as vitamin B6 and allantoin announced over time [3]. Niacinamide is described in dermatology literature as reducing the transfer of pigment to skin cells, which is the basis of its brightening reputation [4].
Variants include face creams, face washes, serums, BB cream and sun-protection versions [4].
Hindustan Unilever launched Fair & Lovely in India in 1975, and it later spread through South Asia, the Middle East and parts of Africa [3][4]. A men's version was added in later decades [4].

On 25 June 2020 the company announced a rebrand, and on 2 July 2020 the product became Glow & Lovely, with words such as "fair" and "lightening" removed from packaging and marketing [4]. The company stated the product is not a bleaching product [3].

Critics have argued that the brand's earlier advertising linked lighter skin with success, employment and marriage, and that the rename did not change this association [3][4]. Defenders point to long-standing local preferences for lighter skin and to consumer demand [4].
A 2025 qualitative study of 15 young British South Asian women explored how pressure to be "Fair and Lovely" contributes to body dissatisfaction and disordered eating [10].

Several animal studies examined Fair & Lovely samples bought in Saudi Arabia. The cream contained about 0.3 micrograms of mercury per gram, below FDA limits, yet treated mice showed mercury in kidney, liver and brain tissue and histological changes, and the authors flagged possible toxicity [7][9]. A later mouse study found mercury accumulation in the ovaries after repeated application, higher than in untreated animals but far lower than for a comparison cream with high mercury content [6].

These studies concern older samples tested in mice and do not describe current formulas. Reports say a 2020 Norwegian restriction cited mercury and hydroquinone levels, which Hindustan Unilever attributed to counterfeit goods [4].

A 2019 clinical imaging study used laser biospeckle to track blood flow on the back of the hand after applying four creams; blood flow rose after all of them and was highest for Fair & Lovely [1]. A rabbit skin study of cosmetics used in an Ethiopian town included Fair and Lovely in irritation testing [8]. No controlled trials of the cream's effect on skin tone appear in the published literature reviewed here.

timeline.event: Hindustan Unilever launches Fair & Lovely in India [3].
Mouse study compares mercury tissue levels after Fair & Lovely and another cream [9].
Brand renamed Glow & Lovely in July; men's line becomes Glow & Handsome [4].
